name: Ford Motor
description: Ford builds and sells Ford and Lincoln vehicles (4.4 million wholesale in 2025) through mostly independent dealers, and earns money in four slices: Ford Blue (petrol and hybrid vehicles for retail buyers, 54 percent of revenue), Ford Pro (trucks and vans for commercial, government and rental customers, 35 percent and by far the most profitable per dollar of sales), Ford Model e (electric vehicles, which lost $4.8 billion on $6.7 billion of revenue) and Ford Credit (auto loans and leases, 7 percent of revenue). 2025 revenue was $187.3 billion (+1%), company adjusted EBIT $6.8 billion (3.6 percent margin, down from 10.2 billion) and net loss $8.2 billion after $17.4 billion of special charges, mainly the Model e impairment and EV program cancellations announced in December 2025.

employees.note: 169 thousand: 163 thousand excluding Ford Credit (87 US, 76 rest of world) plus 6 thousand at Ford Credit (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Ford Blue
businessLines.how: One-time sale of each vehicle to a dealer (revenue booked when shipped to the dealer) plus parts and accessories; profit depends on volume, price mix of trucks and SUVs, and warranty and tariff costs.
businessLines.description: Ford and Lincoln internal-combustion and hybrid vehicles, parts, accessories and digital services for retail customers; all sales in markets outside Ford Pro or Model e scope

businessLines.name: Ford Pro
businessLines.how: Fleet and business customers buy trucks and vans, then keep paying for parts, service and connected-vehicle software; 10.3% margin vs 3.0% in Ford Blue.
businessLines.description: Ford and Lincoln vehicles (Super Duty, Transit range, Ranger in Europe), parts, accessories and services for commercial, government and rental customers

businessLines.name: Ford Model e
businessLines.how: Same dealer-sale model as Blue but at a loss on every vehicle plus heavy development spend; in December 2025 Ford cancelled three planned EVs and ended F-150 Lightning production.
businessLines.description: Ford electric vehicles (including extended-range EVs), parts, accessories and digital services; EV and digital development costs

businessLines.name: Ford Credit
businessLines.how: Interest and lease income on about $146 billion of receivables, financed by its own borrowing; a spread business, not manufacturing.
businessLines.description: Captive finance arm: retail instalment loans and leases to Ford customers and wholesale (floorplan) loans to dealers
